## Mutation ledger (AC5) -- every oracle proven able to fail

Each mutation was applied to the real reader source (all three readers at once, since the
loop is hand-rolled three times), the targeted module re-run, then the file restored from
a byte-for-byte backup. No AttributeError / ImportError verdicts -- every RED below is an
AssertionError from an oracle, naming the truncation.

MUTATED: unconditional `break` at the end of the cursor loop (stop after page one, both
stop conditions and the advance removed).
FAILED: 18 tests. Exact messages included
  * test_reader_recovers_every_seeded_issue_across_three_pages[get_parent_map] --
    "get_parent_map recovered 100 of 250 issues -- the whole-project map is TRUNCATED, so
    issues past the first page look parentless / comment-less / link-less to the differ.
    Missing: ['DIG-100', 'DIG-101', ...]" (same for get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map)
  * test_a_short_page_does_not_terminate_the_walk[get_parent_map] -- "get_parent_map
    recovered 40 of 250 against a server capping pages at 40: a SHORT page was mistaken
    for the LAST page"
  * test_an_exhausted_cursor_alone_terminates_the_walk[null-token-get_parent_map] --
    "get_parent_map/null-token recovered 100"
  * test_islast_alone_terminates_the_walk[get_parent_map] -- "recovered 100 of 250 --
    truncated before isLast"

MUTATED: `if resp.get("isLast") or len(issues) < page_size: break` -- the exact DC bug
(break on a SHORT page) transplanted into Cloud.
FAILED: 3 tests, test_a_short_page_does_not_terminate_the_walk[all three readers] --
"get_comment_map recovered 40 of 250 against a server capping pages at 40: a SHORT page
was mistaken for the LAST page". Note this mutation is invisible to every other oracle,
which is exactly why the short-page server variant is in the module.

MUTATED: never echo the cursor back (`if False: body["nextPageToken"] = ...`).
FAILED: 21 tests, including the dedicated cursor oracle
test_the_cursor_token_advances_across_requests[get_comment_map] -- "get_comment_map
request 1 carried cursor None but response 0 handed back 'cursor:100' -- the cursor did
not advance".

MUTATED: remove the null-cursor stop, leaving only `isLast`.
FAILED: exactly the 6 test_an_exhausted_cursor_alone_terminates_the_walk cases
(absent-token and null-token x 3 readers) -- "get_comment_map issued 26 requests for 3
pages: an exhausted (absent-token) cursor did NOT stop the walk -- it kept re-requesting,
which on a live server is an unbounded spin against Jira". No other oracle catches this,
which is the point of asserting the two stop conditions independently.

MUTATED: remove the `isLast` stop, leaving only the token check.
FAILED: 18 tests, including test_islast_alone_terminates_the_walk[get_parent_map] --
"get_parent_map kept paging past isLast: 26 requests" and
test_the_cursor_token_advances_across_requests -- "re-sent a cursor token:
['cursor:100', 'cursor:200', 'cursor:250', 'cursor:250', ...]".

MUTATED: add a FOURTH whole-project reader to acli_graph.py (get_status_map) that POSTs
/rest/api/3/search/jql once with no cursor loop -- the scenario AC6 exists to prevent.
FAILED: test_no_cloud_whole_project_reader_skips_the_cursor_loop -- "function(s) in
adapters/jira POST /rest/api/3/search/jql without a nextPageToken cursor loop and will
silently return only the FIRST page: ['acli_graph.py:get_status_map (line 475)']".

MUTATED: drift the guard's own file glob from "*.py" to "*.pyx" (i.e. the guard scans
nothing and passes vacuously -- the failure mode that lets a structural guard rot).
FAILED: test_the_structural_guard_actually_sees_the_three_known_readers -- "the guard's
own source list does not include acli_graph.py -- it scanned [], so the whole guard is
VACUOUS". Note the guard test itself stays GREEN under this mutation, which is why the
coverage teeth test exists.

### Note on hang-proofing, which is load-bearing here

Two of the mutations above (drop either stop condition) make the reader re-request the
same offset FOREVER on a live server; the mutant would hang the suite rather than fail.
The fake server therefore raises after 25 requests with "the walk never terminated: N
requests for M issues -- the cursor loop is spinning". The readers' fail-open
`except Exception` converts that into their silent-partial-map path, which is precisely
what the recovered-set and request-count oracles then report -- so the mutation surfaces
as a named RED instead of a timeout. That same fail-open swallow is the second-order
effect described in the defect ticket below.

### Existing assertions

None weakened. The prior single-page coverage in
mutate/test_acli_cross_mixin_binding.py:188,200 is untouched and still passes (52 passed
across the new module + that module + the DC pagination module).
